name: Money Drawing Candle Dressing
purpose: Draws steady income, new money and prosperity toward you.
description: In hoodoo and Southern conjure, a candle is often 'dressed' with a condition oil such as Money Drawing Oil and a little powdered herb before it is lit, so the burning carries the prayer. Green is the color of paper money in the United States and gold suggests coin, which is why both are favored for money work. Basil and allspice are long-standing money herbs in American folk magic.

oils.amount: or 2 drops in 1 tsp carrier oil

herbs.amount: a light pinch
a pinch, in a ring on the plate only
a pinch, in the ring on the plate

extras.item: Petition paper with the amount you need
extras.amount: 1, folded toward you and placed under the plate

direction: To draw, stroke the oil from just below the top half inch down toward the base, moving toward you, and from the base up toward the middle, so both ends pull toward your body.
carving: A dollar sign near the top and your name down the side.
steps: Wipe the candle with a dry cloth and state the specific money you need, such as a bill paid or a new client.
Carve your name down the side and a dollar sign near the top, keeping the blade moving away from your hand.
Warm 3 drops of Money Drawing Oil, or the diluted basil blend, between your palms and stroke it on toward you, avoiding the wick and the top half inch.
Wipe off the excess, then pat a light film of ground basil on the lower third only.
Write your petition, fold it toward you and set it under the heatproof plate, then place the pyrite beside the holder.
Sprinkle the cinnamon and allspice in a ring on the plate at least an inch from the candle and light it while you speak the words.
Burn for 15 to 30 minutes while you sit with the flame and think of practical steps, then snuff it and relight it on following Thursdays or daily until it is done.
words:
Green to grow and gold to shine,
fair money come and settle mine.
By honest work and open door,
this flame calls plenty, more and more.
bestTime: Waxing moon, on a Thursday or Sunday
caution: Never leave the candle burning unattended or while you sleep; if you want it to burn down over several sessions, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it next time. Set it in a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, because too much oil can make the flame flare. Wash your hands after dressing, and never put essential oils neat on skin or on broken skin. Never roll the candle in loose herbs: dust only a light film of finely ground herb on the lower part of the candle, or keep the herbs in a ring on the plate, and watch the flame the whole time with a snuffer or lid and water nearby. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Ventilate the room, keep glitter, paper and plastic off the candle itself, and snuff or smother a flare rather than throwing water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before disposal and never pour hot wax down a drain. Formula oils such as Money Drawing Oil often contain cinnamon or other warming oils, so patch test and keep them off your face. Basil essential oil contains estragole and is best avoided in pregnancy, while breastfeeding and on children; use the formula oil or a carrier alone instead. Ground cinnamon and allspice can irritate skin and eyes, which is why they stay on the plate. Sweet almond carrier oil is a nut oil, so choose jojoba if you have a nut allergy.
pets: Basil is listed by the ASPCA as non-toxic to cats and dogs, but essential oils, cinnamon and allspice can irritate pets. Keep the lit candle, the dressing oil and the herb plate away from pets, and do not diffuse or leave essential oils where a cat can touch or lick them, since cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Love Attraction Candle Dressing
purpose: Opens your life to new, mutual love without naming or binding any one person.
description: Pink and red candles dressed with rose and an attraction oil are common in both hoodoo and modern witchcraft for drawing romance. Rose has been linked with love goddesses such as Aphrodite and Venus since antiquity, and lavender is a gentle, friendly love herb in European folk lore. This dressing asks for a partner who is free and willing, rather than aiming at a particular person.

oils.amount: or 2 drops in 1 tsp carrier oil

herbs.amount: a light pinch
a pinch, in a ring on the plate

extras.item: Petition listing the qualities you want in a partner

direction: Draw the oil from the top area down toward the base, moving toward your heart, so the candle pulls love inward.
carving: A heart on one side and a word such as 'kindness' or 'joy' on the other.
steps: Write the qualities you want in a partner, such as honesty and humor, without naming anyone, and fold the paper toward you.
Carve a heart and one quality word into the candle.
Dress the candle with 3 drops of Come to Me Oil or the diluted rose geranium blend, stroking toward you and keeping clear of the wick and top half inch.
Wipe away the excess and press a light dusting of ground rose petals onto the lower third.
Set the petition under the plate, ring the base with ground lavender at least an inch away, and place the rose quartz nearby.
Light the candle, speak the words, and spend a few minutes imagining how it feels to be loved well.
Snuff it after 15 to 30 minutes and relight on the next Friday or each evening until the candle is finished.
words:
Rose of the heart and flame of the sun,
call to me love that is free and is won.
Given with gladness and offered by choice,
let my true match hear my voice.
bestTime: Waxing to full moon, on a Friday
caution: Never leave the candle burning unattended or while you sleep; if you want it to burn down over several sessions, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it next time. Set it in a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, because too much oil can make the flame flare. Wash your hands after dressing, and never put essential oils neat on skin or on broken skin. Never roll the candle in loose herbs: dust only a light film of finely ground herb on the lower part of the candle, or keep the herbs in a ring on the plate, and watch the flame the whole time with a snuffer or lid and water nearby. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Ventilate the room, keep glitter, paper and plastic off the candle itself, and snuff or smother a flare rather than throwing water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before disposal and never pour hot wax down a drain. Come to Me Oil and other attraction formulas vary by maker, so patch test on the inside of your arm first. Rose geranium oil can irritate sensitive skin and is commonly advised against in early pregnancy without professional advice. Lavender can cause skin allergy in a few people. Respect consent: this dressing invites love, it does not target someone's will.
pets: The ASPCA lists lavender as toxic to cats, dogs and horses, so keep the herb ring and candle where pets cannot nibble or knock it. Keep the lit candle, the dressing oil and the herb plate away from pets, and do not diffuse or leave essential oils where a cat can touch or lick them, since cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Self-Love Candle Dressing
purpose: Builds self-worth, kindness toward yourself and a softer inner voice.
description: Self-love candles are a modern witchcraft practice that borrows the rose and pink color symbolism of love magic and turns it toward the self. Chamomile is a traditional soothing herb in European herbalism, and rose quartz is widely used today as a stone of gentle love. Carving your own name makes you the one the candle draws love toward.

oils.amount: or 1 drop in 1 tsp carrier oil
plus 1 drop in the same tsp of carrier oil

herbs.amount: a light pinch
a pinch, in a ring on the plate

direction: Stroke the oil toward you from top to bottom while saying something kind about yourself with each stroke.
carving: Your own name with a small heart around it.
steps: Sit somewhere quiet and write down three things you appreciate about yourself.
Carve your name and a heart around it into the candle.
Dress the candle with 3 drops of Love Me Now Self-Love Oil or the diluted palmarosa and lavender blend, stroking toward you and staying below the top half inch.
Wipe off the extra oil and dust the lower third lightly with ground rose petals.
Ring the base with chamomile on the plate, set the rose quartz beside it and prop the mirror well away from the flame.
Light the candle, look at yourself in the mirror and say the words aloud.
Burn for up to 30 minutes, read your three appreciations, then snuff the candle and repeat each morning or evening for a week.
words:
Flame of rose, warm and true,
teach me the love I owe to you.
Gentle in word and kind in eye,
I am worth loving, you and I.
bestTime: Waxing moon, on a Friday or Monday
caution: Never leave the candle burning unattended or while you sleep; if you want it to burn down over several sessions, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it next time. Set it in a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, because too much oil can make the flame flare. Wash your hands after dressing, and never put essential oils neat on skin or on broken skin. Never roll the candle in loose herbs: dust only a light film of finely ground herb on the lower part of the candle, or keep the herbs in a ring on the plate, and watch the flame the whole time with a snuffer or lid and water nearby. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Ventilate the room, keep glitter, paper and plastic off the candle itself, and snuff or smother a flare rather than throwing water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before disposal and never pour hot wax down a drain. Chamomile can trigger allergy in people sensitive to ragweed, daisies or marigolds. Lavender and palmarosa are generally mild at this dilution but can still irritate sensitive skin, so patch test; ask a qualified practitioner before using essential oils in pregnancy. Sweet almond is a nut oil, so use jojoba if you have a nut allergy. Keep the mirror out of direct sunlight near the candle.
pets: The ASPCA lists both chamomile and lavender as toxic to cats, dogs and horses, so keep the plate and candle out of reach. Keep the lit candle, the dressing oil and the herb plate away from pets, and do not diffuse or leave essential oils where a cat can touch or lick them, since cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Protection Candle Dressing
purpose: Raises a protective boundary around you, your home or your work.
description: Fiery Wall of Protection is a well-known hoodoo formula used to dress candles that guard a person or household. Rosemary and bay laurel have protective reputations across European and Mediterranean folk tradition, and black tourmaline is a popular modern protection stone. Black absorbs and blocks, while white adds blessing.

oils.amount: or 2 drops in 1 tsp carrier oil

herbs.amount: a light pinch
a pinch, in a ring on the plate

extras.amount: 1, at the front of the plate
a thin circle around the plate

direction: Start at the middle of the candle and stroke outward to both ends, as if pushing a wall out around you, stopping below the top half inch.
carving: A pentacle or a simple shield shape, with your name or address below it.
steps: Decide exactly what the candle is guarding: you, your family, your home or your car.
Carve the pentacle or shield and the name or address underneath.
Dress from the center outward with 3 drops of Fiery Wall of Protection Oil or the diluted frankincense blend, keeping off the wick and top half inch.
Wipe off any excess and dust the lower third lightly with ground rosemary.
Ring the plate with bay laurel, then lay a thin circle of salt around the outside of the plate and set the black tourmaline in front.
Light the candle and say the words three times, picturing a ring of firelight around what you protect.
Snuff after 20 to 30 minutes and relight nightly through the waning moon, or whenever you feel the need.
words:
Ring of fire, wall of light,
guard my door by day and night.
What comes in harm, turn round and go;
only good may cross this glow.
bestTime: Waning moon or full moon, on a Saturday or Tuesday
caution: Never leave the candle burning unattended or while you sleep; if you want it to burn down over several sessions, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it next time. Wash your hands after dressing, and never put essential oils neat on skin or on broken skin. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Ventilate the room, keep glitter, paper and plastic off the candle itself, and snuff or smother a flare rather than throwing water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before disposal and never pour hot wax down a drain. Fiery Wall of Protection formulas are traditionally 'hot' and may contain cinnamon, pepper or similar irritating oils, so use gloves or a cotton swab, patch test and keep it away from eyes and children. Bay laurel and frankincense can cause skin sensitivity in some people. Rosemary is safe as a dried herb, but rosemary essential oil is not used here and is best avoided in pregnancy and epilepsy. Keep the salt dry and swept away afterward.
pets: The ASPCA lists bay laurel as toxic to cats, dogs and horses, and salt is harmful if pets lick large amounts, so sweep up afterward. Keep the lit candle, the dressing oil and the herb plate away from pets, and do not diffuse or leave essential oils where a cat can touch or lick them, since cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Uncrossing and Curse Breaking Candle Dressing
purpose: Lifts a run of bad luck, a jinx or a feeling of being crossed.
description: In hoodoo, a person who feels jinxed or 'crossed' may burn a white or purple candle dressed with Uncrossing Oil while reading Psalm 51, which asks to be purged with hyssop and washed clean. Hyssop and agrimony are both old cleansing and hex-returning herbs in European and American folk practice. The oil is stroked away from the body to pull the trouble off.

herbs.amount: a light pinch
a pinch, in a ring on the plate

extras.amount: a thin circle around the plate

direction: Stroke from just below the top half inch down to the base, moving away from your body, as if wiping the crossed condition off and away.
carving: Your name, with an equal-armed cross above it.
steps: Take a shower or wash your hands and face first, as a fresh start.
Carve your name and an equal-armed cross above it.
Dress with 3 drops of Uncrossing Oil or Jinx Removing Oil, stroking downward and away from you and staying below the top half inch.
Wipe off the excess and dust the lower third lightly with ground hyssop.
Ring the plate with agrimony, circle it with salt and set the glass of water beside it to collect what is lifted.
Light the candle and read Psalm 51 or speak the words, picturing the heaviness draining into the water.
Snuff the candle after 20 to 30 minutes and pour the water down an outdoor drain or onto the ground away from your door; repeat for seven days on a fresh glass of water.
words:
What was crossed is now made straight,
what was bound is free of weight.
Hyssop clean and flame of white,
lift this jinx and set me right.
caution: Never leave the candle burning unattended or while you sleep; if you want it to burn down over several sessions, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it next time. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Ventilate the room, keep glitter, paper and plastic off the candle itself, and snuff or smother a flare rather than throwing water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before disposal and never pour hot wax down a drain. Uncrossing and jinx-removing formulas vary and may include hyssop or citrus oils; patch test, and avoid sunlight on oiled skin if the label lists citrus. Hyssop is not taken internally here and is best avoided in pregnancy and by people with epilepsy, so pregnant people can leave the herb on the plate rather than on the candle. Do not drink the water. If you feel unwell or persistently unlucky, also speak with someone you trust or a professional.
pets: Keep the glass of water out of pets' reach so they do not drink it, and sweep up the salt afterward. Keep the lit candle, the dressing oil and the herb plate away from pets, and do not diffuse or leave essential oils where a cat can touch or lick them, since cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Banishing Candle Dressing
purpose: Sends away an unwanted habit, influence or situation.
description: Banishing candles are traditionally black and burned on a waning moon, when lore says things shrink and depart. Black pepper and cedar have both been used in folk magic to drive off and clear. This dressing banishes a situation or influence, never a person's wellbeing.

oils.amount: or 1 drop in 1 tsp carrier oil
plus 1 drop in the same tsp of carrier oil

herbs.amount: a light pinch
a pinch, in a ring on the plate only

extras.item: Paper naming the habit or situation
extras.amount: 1, folded away from you and kept under the plate

direction: Stroke from the base up toward the top half inch, moving away from your body, so the candle pushes the unwanted thing out and away.
carving: The habit or situation in a word, with a line through it.
steps: Name the habit, influence or situation you are ending, in a word or short phrase.
Carve the word into the candle and draw a line through it.
Dress with 3 drops of Banishing Oil or the diluted pepper and cypress blend, stroking away from you and keeping clear of the wick and top half inch.
Wipe off the excess and dust the lower third lightly with ground cedar.
Fold the paper away from you, set it under the plate and ring the base with ground black pepper at least an inch from the candle.
Light the candle, speak the words and picture the thing growing smaller as the candle burns down.
Snuff it after 20 to 30 minutes and relight nightly until the moon is dark; take the cooled wax remains and the paper out of the house to the trash.
words:
Waning moon and candle black,
take this thing and don't send it back.
Smaller, fainter, gone from me,
as I will, so mote it be.

Cypress oil is generally mild, but ask a qualified practitioner before using essential oils in pregnancy. Banishing work should target habits and situations, not harm another person.
pets: Ground pepper can irritate pets' noses and mouths if sniffed or licked. Keep the lit candle, the dressing oil and the herb plate away from pets, and do not diffuse or leave essential oils where a cat can touch or lick them, since cats are especially sensitive to essential oils.

name: Road Opening Candle Dressing
purpose: Clears blocks and opens new paths in work, travel or life.
description: Road Opener Oil is a hoodoo formula for removing obstacles, and in Latin American folk practice the name abre camino ('opens the way') is given to plants and products for the same purpose. Orange and yellow candles are often chosen for opportunity and movement. Lemongrass and orange peel are bright, clearing scents that fit the work.

oils.amount: or 2 drops in 1 tsp carrier oil

herbs.amount: a light pinch
a pinch, in a ring on the plate

extras.amount: 1, laid in front of the plate pointing away from you

direction: Stroke from the base upward toward the top half inch, as if clearing the road ahead, then once more toward you to bring the opening home.
carving: An arrow pointing up, or a small key shape.
steps: Name the road you want opened, such as a job search, a move or a creative project.
Carve an upward arrow or key shape into the candle.
Dress with 3 drops of Road Opener Oil or the diluted sweet orange blend, stroking from the base upward and keeping off the wick and top half inch.
Wipe off the excess and dust the lower third lightly with ground lemongrass.
Ring the plate with orange peel and lay the key in front, pointing away from you.
Light the candle and speak the words, then write down one action you will take this week.
Snuff it after 20 to 30 minutes and relight each morning for a week, taking the action between sessions.
words:
Gate swing wide and path run clear,
what blocked my way is gone from here.
Key in hand and flame to guide,
open roads on every side.

name: Healing Support Candle Dressing
purpose: Sends comfort and strength to someone recovering, alongside their medical care.
description: Blue and white candles are used in many modern and folk traditions to send peace and wellbeing to the sick. Calendula and lemon balm are gentle, sunny herbs with long histories in European herbal lore. This candle supports healing in spirit and never replaces a doctor or treatment.

oils.amount: or 2 drops in 1 tsp carrier oil

herbs.amount: a light pinch
a pinch, in a ring on the plate

extras.item: Paper with the person's name, written with their permission

direction: Stroke from the top area down toward the base and toward you, drawing in health, comfort and strength.
carving: The person's name and a small sun or equal-armed cross.
steps: Ask the person if they would like you to light a candle for them, and respect their answer.
Carve their name (or yours) and a small sun into the candle.
Dress with 3 drops of Healing Oil or the diluted lavender blend, stroking toward you and keeping off the wick and top half inch.
Wipe off the excess and pat a light dusting of ground calendula on the lower third.
Set the name paper under the plate, ring the base with lemon balm and place the clear quartz beside it.
Light the candle, speak the words and picture the person resting comfortably and well cared for.
Snuff it after 15 to 30 minutes and relight daily for as long as they are recovering.
words:
Gentle flame of blue and white,
ease the body, bring the light.
Rest and mend and heal and grow,
comfort be where this flame glows.

name: Peace in the Home Candle Dressing
purpose: Calms tension and arguments and brings a gentle mood to the household.
description: Peaceful Home and Peace Water style formulas are used in hoodoo to cool a quarrelsome house, often with soft blue or white candles. Lavender and lemon balm are calming herbs in European folk herbalism, and blue lace agate is a modern favorite for calm speech. Spreading the oil from the center outward lets the peace move through every room.

oils.amount: or 1 drop in 1 tsp carrier oil
plus 1 drop in the same tsp of carrier oil

herbs.amount: a light pinch
a pinch, in a ring on the plate

extras.item: Paper with your household's first names

direction: Begin at the middle of the candle and stroke gently outward to each end, letting calm spread out to every corner of the home.
carving: The word 'peace', or a dove, with a circle around it.
steps: Tidy the room you will use, open a window a little and take three slow breaths.
Carve the word 'peace' or a dove inside a circle.
Dress from the center outward with 3 drops of Peaceful Home Oil or the diluted lavender and chamomile blend, avoiding the wick and top half inch.
Wipe off the excess and dust the lower third lightly with ground lavender.
Set the names paper under the plate, ring the base with lemon balm and place the blue lace agate beside it.
Light the candle in a central room where people gather, and speak the words softly.
Snuff it after 20 to 30 minutes and relight in the evenings, especially after a hard day.
words:
Soft as water, still as stone,
peace come settle in this home.
Harsh words fade and tempers mend,
each to each a gentle friend.

Set it in a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. A candle supports calm; if anyone is unsafe at home, reach out for help.

name: Psychic Vision and Dreams Candle Dressing
purpose: Opens intuition and invites clear, memorable dreams before sleep.
description: Mugwort is one of the best-known dream and seeing herbs in European folklore, and purple or silver candles are used in modern witchcraft for intuition and the moon. Psychic Vision formulas are dressed on candles before divination or dreamwork. This candle is lit before bed and snuffed before you lie down, never left burning while you sleep.

herbs.amount: a pinch, in a ring on the plate
a small pinch, in the ring on the plate

direction: Stroke from the base upward toward the top half inch, raising your sight, then wipe off the excess.
carving: An open eye with a crescent moon above it.
steps: About an hour before bed, dim the lights and set your dream journal by the bed.
Carve an open eye with a crescent above it.
Dress with 3 drops of Psychic Vision Oil or Sleep and Dreams Oil, stroking upward and keeping off the wick and top half inch.
Wipe off the excess, and ring the base with ground mugwort and star anise on the plate, at least an inch from the candle.
Hold the amethyst or moonstone, light the candle and speak the words while gazing softly at the flame.
After 15 to 20 minutes, snuff the candle fully and check that it is out before you go to bed; tuck the stone under your pillow.
On waking, write down any dreams before you get up, and repeat on following nights.
words:
Silver moon and violet flame,
show me true and speak my name.
What I dream, let me recall,
open sight and clear for all.
bestTime: Full moon, on a Monday night
caution: Never leave the candle burning unattended or while you sleep; if you want it to burn down over several sessions, snuff it (do not blow it out) and relight it next time. Set it in a sturdy holder on a heatproof plate or tray, at least 12 inches from curtains, paper, plants and anything that can burn, out of reach of children and pets, and tie back long hair and loose sleeves. Use only a few drops of dressing oil, wipe off the excess, and keep oil off the wick and the top half inch of the candle, because too much oil can make the flame flare. Wash your hands after dressing, and never put essential oils neat on skin or on broken skin. Never roll the candle in loose herbs: dust only a light film of finely ground herb on the lower part of the candle, or keep the herbs in a ring on the plate, and watch the flame the whole time with a snuffer or lid and water nearby. Carve away from your hand with a toothpick, pin or blunt tool. Ventilate the room, keep glitter, paper and plastic off the candle itself, and snuff or smother a flare rather than throwing water on hot wax or a wax fire. Let the wax cool completely before disposal and never pour hot wax down a drain. Always snuff this candle before sleep and never take it into the bedroom to burn overnight. Mugwort should be avoided in pregnancy and can cause allergy in people sensitive to ragweed, daisies or celery; pregnant people should leave it out. Real star anise is fine on the plate, but never eat it, since Japanese star anise looks similar and is toxic. Psychic and dream formulas may contain oils such as clary sage that are best avoided in pregnancy, so check the label and patch test.

name: Success and Victory Candle Dressing
purpose: Boosts confidence and favor for a goal, contest, interview or launch.
description: Crown of Success is a hoodoo formula for mastery and recognition, and High John the Conqueror root is a famous American conjure charm for victory and personal power. a pinch, in a ring on the plate

Carve a crown or wreath and one word for the goal.
Dress with 3 drops of Crown of Success Oil or Success Oil, stroking toward you and keeping off the wick and top half inch.
Wipe off the excess and dust the lower third lightly with ground bay laurel.
Place the petition under the plate, ring the base with sunflower petals and set the High John root beside the holder.
Light the candle, hold the root, and speak the words while picturing the moment you succeed.
Snuff it after 20 to 30 minutes and relight daily until the event; carry the root in a pocket on the day.

Laurel bright and golden crown,
lift me up and don't let down.
Skill and nerve and favor true,
victory come in all I do.

name: Lucky Break Candle Dressing
purpose: Invites good luck, lucky timing and fortunate chances.
description: Fast Luck and Lucky Hand are classic hoodoo formulas, and chamomile is traditionally used by gamblers in American folk magic to wash the hands before play. Green aventurine is a modern 'lucky' stone. Green and orange candles speak to fortune and good timing.

a pinch, in a ring on the plate only

extras.amount: 1, set in front of the candle

carving: A four-leaf clover or the number 7.

Carve a four-leaf clover or the number 7.
Dress with 3 drops of Fast Luck Oil or Lucky Hand Oil, stroking toward you from both ends and avoiding the wick and top half inch.
Wipe off the excess and dust the lower third lightly with ground chamomile.
Ring the plate with ground allspice, set the green aventurine beside it and the coin in front.
Light the candle and speak the words seven times.
Snuff it after 15 to 30 minutes and relight on lucky days; carry the coin with you when you need the luck.

Lucky flame and clover green,
bring me chances yet unseen.
Right on time and right in place,
fortune smile upon my face.

description: Thyme was linked with courage in medieval Europe, where tradition says ladies embroidered sprigs on the scarves of knights. Ginger is a warming herb used in many folk traditions to add fire and speed to a working. Red and orange candles carry the heat of bravery, and carnelian is a modern stone for confidence.

Snuff it after 15 to 20 minutes and carry the stone with you; relight before each challenge.

Fire in belly, iron in spine,
brave of heart and bold in line.
Fear may come but will not stay;
I rise up and walk my way.

purpose: Clears stale or heavy energy from yourself or a space.
description: Van Van Oil is a New Orleans hoodoo formula, traditionally lemongrass-based, used to clear away bad conditions and refresh a space. Dress with 3 drops of Van Van Oil or Blessing Oil, stroking downward and away from you and avoiding the wick and top half inch.

Salt and sage and rosemary,
wash this place and set it free.
What is stale, now blow away;

Those who walked the road before,
welcome to my light and door.

purpose: Softens hard feelings and opens the way to an honest, kind conversation.
description: Sweetening is a hoodoo practice that uses sugar, honey and gentle oils to make a situation kinder, and Reconciliation Oil is dressed on candles to heal quarrels between friends, family or partners.
